# Problem-Solving Field Guide

The verifier grades files, not reasoning. Write
the output artifact early and update it continuously.

## Starting posture

Before any action: identify the exact output
artifact, read all referenced source material,
trace what the verifier will execute, and copy
every mutable resource.

One-paragraph plan. Then act. Planning that
consumes turns without writing files is the
primary failure mode.

Save at 60% confidence. Read failures literally.
Fix the specific named thing. Three identical
structural failures means the structure is wrong.

## How to trace a rejection to its cause

When a component rejects input that should be
valid, the error message names the rejection site.
Search the source for that exact string. It lands
on the raising line. Trace one level up to the
classification logic — the predicate, regex, or
comparison that decided the input was invalid.

Identify the gap between what the classifier
accepts and what the input presents. The gap is
almost always narrow: a missing alternative, a
case-sensitivity assumption, a single flag. Close
it with the smallest possible change.

Do not restructure surrounding code. Every extra
line touched is a new surface for regressions.
Verify that the formerly-failing input now passes
and the formerly-passing input still passes.

## How to produce a diff deliverable

When the output artifact is a patch or diff,
generate it from the version-control tooling after
editing the source file. Do not write unified diffs
by hand — context-line counts must be exact or the
patch will be rejected by the application tool.

Verify the patch applies cleanly to an unmodified
copy of the tree. The patch file must exist at the
exact path the spec names — a correct diff at the
wrong location scores zero.

## How to restore an unreadable file

When an engine refuses to open a file and the bytes
appear random or corrupted, look for a transform
key in the surrounding environment before attempting
to parse the binary format manually.

Search configuration files, nearby source files,
and environment definitions for a key, passphrase,
or simple transform constant. Apply it to a working
copy of the file. Let the engine open the restored
copy — the engine's own parser is more reliable
than a hand-rolled one and handles edge cases
automatically.

For compressed or archived data: identify the
format from the file's leading bytes, decompress
with the standard library, then parse the inner
content.

## How to preserve mutable resources

Many resources change state on first access:

- Databases with associated log files: opening the
  database — even for a read-only query — can merge
  the log into the main file and delete the log.
  Copy the main file and every associated sidecar
  before any client invocation.
- Repositories: maintenance and network operations
  can discard unreachable history. Inspect the full
  local object graph — including reflogs and loose
  objects — before running any such operation.
- Programs with stateful startup: inspect bytes and
  strings before executing.

## How to verify lifecycle correctness

When a task requires cleanup to run on interruption,
verify it by actually interrupting the process and
observing the cleanup output. Do not reason that
cleanup should run — measure that it does. Cleanup
paths must be reachable from every exit route.

## How to confirm a service is running

A script that starts a process must confirm the
process is actually serving before it exits. Validate
configuration first. Start the process. Poll the
interface the verifier will check. Do not exit until
the poll succeeds.

Match every spec detail: field names, delimiters,
format strings, port numbers. Structured output
formats are fragile — a single missing separator
causes all downstream pattern matching to fail.

## How to work within output size constraints

When the artifact has a size cap, encode a generator
rather than embedding data. Use deterministic,
closed-form computation per output unit. Methods
that sample many times per unit will exceed time
limits on large outputs.

The artifact must be self-contained. It cannot read
external files at runtime if those files will not
be present in the verifier's environment.

## How to investigate an unknown program

Work from cheapest to most expensive: list the
working directory, read bytes and printable strings,
request help output, run with minimal input and
observe all output channels, trace system calls.

When user input is passed as a format string rather
than as a format argument, format specifiers in the
input cause the program to read and print adjacent
memory.

## Spec compliance

Literal values — dates, paths, field names, output
schemas — are hard constraints. Reproduce them
exactly. A pinned date is never a runtime clock
call. State interval boundary semantics explicitly.
Match sample output format character for character.

## Tools

Shell, Python, file I/O. No speculative imports of
packages that may not be installed.

## Code hygiene

Smallest patch. Monotonic clock for timing. Shrink
path for growing containers. Validate at boundaries.
Comments for non-obvious reasons only.

## Before stopping

Re-read the artifact. If it does not match your
current understanding, update it. The file's state
at termination is the only thing graded.
